derniere_question.enonce: A bank runs an ADK agent on Cloud Run. Security asks to block prompt injection attempts in user messages before they reach the model, without changing the agent code. What should the architect recommend?

options.A: Create a VPC Service Controls perimeter around Vertex AI.
options.B: Enable Model Armor with a prompt template through the ADK Model Armor plugin.
options.C: Put Cloud Armor in front of the Cloud Run service.
options.D: Add a regular expression filter in the agent instruction.

derniere_question.explication: Model Armor inspects prompts and responses for injection and jailbreak attempts; the ADK plugin applies it without changing agent logic.

pieges.A: VPC-SC prevents data exfiltration across perimeters; it does not inspect prompt content.
pieges.C: Cloud Armor filters HTTP traffic at the load balancer, not the semantics of a prompt.
pieges.D: Instructions are not a security control and require changing the agent.

parts.text:
Relis ce code ADK s'il te plaît :

```python
from google.adk.agents import LlmAgent, LoopAgent

def chercher(requete, ctx):
    return {"resultat": requete}

redacteur = LlmAgent(name="redacteur", model="gemini-3.5-flash", tools=[chercher])
relecteur = LlmAgent(name="relecteur", model="gemini-3.5-flash")
root_agent = LoopAgent(name="boucle", sub_agents=[redacteur, relecteur])
```

rubric_content.text_property: The review points out that the LoopAgent has no max_iterations and risks looping indefinitely.
The review points out that the tool function lacks type hints or a docstring.
The review points out that the context parameter should be named tool_context and typed as ToolContext.
